slides.title: An Objection Is a Position, Not an Obstacle
bullets: Any moment of genuine skepticism, disagreement or alternative interpretation of the evidence
A competing trial, a generalisability concern, a different clinical read on the same data
How it's handled is one of the clearest tests of whether exchange is genuine

slides.title: Sales Objection-Handling Doesn't Belong Here
bullets: Most objection-handling literature comes from a sales context built to move toward a purchase
Structurally inappropriate for non-promotional, balanced scientific exchange
Importing it risks exactly the drift from exploring into persuading

slides.title: Reflect Before Responding
bullets: Listen fully and reflect the objection back accurately before responding
Confirms real understanding of what was actually said
Avoids the common failure of answering an easier, different version of the concern

slides.title: Engage With the Substance Honestly
bullets: Acknowledge a concern directly when it is grounded in real data
"That's a fair point, and here's what the evidence does and doesn't tell us"
Scientific credibility depends on not defending every data point reflexively

slides.title: Add Context Without Overclaiming Resolution
bullets: Provide study design or population differences where they genuinely help
Be clear about what is and is not yet known
Don't imply an objection has been overcome if real uncertainty remains

slides.title: Unresolved Is Sometimes the Right Ending
bullets: An objection can end in a captured insight rather than a resolution
A genuine, unresolved scientific disagreement is valuable field intelligence
Flagging the gap internally often beats an improvised answer on the spot

takeaway.title: Objections are handled by listening and engaging honestly, never by overcoming them like a sales pitch
bullets: Reflect the objection accurately before responding to it
Acknowledge real limitations instead of defending every data point
An honest, unresolved disagreement can be more valuable than a improvised answer
